evals.name: salesforce-help-page-js-rendered
evals.expected_output: Skill detects runtime. If a headless browser is available (Playwright via Python or Node, or Edge on Windows 11, or Chrome), uses it. Saves references/help-salesforce-com-service-cloud-voice/{page.html, page.md, meta.json}. The meta.json includes retrieval date. The page.md contains real content, not a near-empty shell. If no headless browser is available, the skill says so plainly using the printed-cookbook-vs-kitchen analogy and offers the ranked install walkthrough.

assertions.rationale: A successful render must produce a non-empty page.md, not just a shell.
meta.json must record the retrieval date so freshness decay can age the citation.
An empty SPA shell means JS did not execute; the runtime selection is wrong.

evals.name: search-subject-salesforce-flavored
evals.expected_output: Skill detects the Salesforce-flavored topic and runs the Salesforce-aware engines (help.salesforce.com, trailhead, architect, developer.salesforce.com) in addition to the general engines (Google, Bing, Scholar). Writes references/_search/agentforce-for-healthcare-patient-services.md with engine attribution. Offers to harvest the top 3-5 results.

assertions.rationale: Salesforce-flavored topic must engage at least one Salesforce-aware engine.
General engines must also run; Salesforce-aware is additive, not replacement.

evals.name: pdf-preference-over-html-crawl
evals.expected_output: Skill detects the linked PDF edition of the Apex Reference Guide and downloads the PDF instead of crawling the multi-page HTML portal. Saves references/<slug>/page.pdf + meta.json. Tells the user the PDF was preferred and why.

assertions.rationale: Full-guide PDF must be preferred over the HTML portal per the Salesforce-doc shortcut map.
User must see why the PDF route was chosen — silent preference is opaque.

evals.name: help-mode-no-fetch
evals.expected_output: Skill prints the user-facing walkthrough: what it does, the headless-browser analogy in plain English, the runtime detection chain, every flag with a worked example, the proactive install offers, the err-doctrine close. Does NOT fetch anything. Does NOT prompt for a URL.

assertions.rationale: Help text must include the runtime analogy users learn from.
Help mode must not fetch anything — no run artifact should appear.

evals.name: empty-page-no-headless-runtime
evals.prompt: /download https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.service_cloud_voice.htm (assume no headless runtime is installed; only curl/wget are available)
evals.expected_output: Skill uses fetch-basic.sh, gets back a near-empty <div id='app'> shell, recognizes the result is incomplete, tells the user using the printed-cookbook-vs-kitchen analogy, and presents the ranked four-option install offer (Python+Playwright / Node+Playwright / Edge on Windows / skip-for-now / never-ask-again). Persists the answer in .install-asked.json.

assertions.rationale: User must understand WHY the result is unusable, not just see a failure.
The ranked install offer must surface concrete runtime options.
Answer must persist so the offer doesn't repeat on every run.
